text: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Updated Exterior Lighting Policy Approved May 17, 2024 (56) Lighting. a. General. DRC approval is required to modify or add exterior lighting. This includes but is not limited to motion detector spotlights, security lighting, landscape lighting, architectural accent lighting, decorative lighting, ballasted fixtures, additional lighting at doors or windows, etc. "Cut sheets" (product description, specifications, and illustrations) must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for each type of fixture proposed for review. 1. All exterior lighting must be compliant with these Rules and Douglas County's "Dark Skies" guidelines (https://www.douglas.co.us/planning/development- review- regulations/development-info-assistance/development-outdoor-lighting/). To minimize the effects of light pollution, lighting should: • Only be on when needed; • Only light the area that needs it; • Be no brighter than necessary • Be used only when needed; • Use warmer color lights where possible. 2. Exterior Lighting Replacement Program: To replace exterior light fixtures on your home, follow the “Five Lighting Principles for Responsible Outdoor Lighting” guidelines in (56) Lighting, a.1. select a fixture where the bulb is fully shielded with the cone of light pointing down to minimize skyglow, glare, and light trespass, and submit an Exterior Lighting Improvement application. 3. Lighting techniques that "up light" buildings or landscapes (trees, shrubs, etc.) and shine light into the sky shall not be permitted. -- 1 of 6 -- Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Updated Exterior Lighting Policy Approved May 17, 2024 4. Exterior light fixtures must be fully shielded so that the lamp bulb or LED cluster is not visible from property lines or the street and have a warm white light with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred). 5. Exterior lighting must be directed downward so that the light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or onto the street. 6. At any time, unduly bright lights that create a nuisance to adjacent owners or lighting complaints received may be re-evaluated. 7. Utilizing photocells and timers to control the switching on and off of site lighting is highly encouraged. 8. Exterior lighting that lights an outdoor living space (such as a patio, porch, or deck) shall light only the livable space and not extend beyond that area. -- 2 of 6 --
summaryText: Resolution No. 2024-05-04, adopted May 17, 2024, amends and replaces Sec. 21-22(b)(56), Lighting, effective immediately. DRC approval is required to modify or add exterior lighting, including motion detector spotlights, security lighting, landscape lighting, architectural accent lighting, decorative lighting, ballasted fixtures, and additional lighting at doors or windows. Cut sheets must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for each type of fixture proposed. All exterior lighting must comply with the Rules and Douglas County Dark Skies guidelines. Exterior lighting must be fully shielded, directed downward, warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less, and may be re-evaluated if it creates nuisance or complaints. Under-eave lighting provides architectural accent lighting. Canned lighting installed into front porch soffits or ceilings is included. Under-eave lighting must consist of hardwired fixtures installed into the soffit or hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems such as Jellyfish or Gemstone. Gemstone and Jellyfish systems are the approved systems. Other similar companies or products are not permitted unless added to the approved list of dark sky-compliant lighting systems. Under-eave lighting may be installed on the front of the home using logical termination points from the front to the sides; elevations showing termination points must be submitted with the application; termination points may not extend further than the wing fence. Under-eave lighting may be installed on the rear of the home if it backs up to open space, subject to DRC approval and case-by-case review. Corner lots can install under-eave lighting on the side of the home that abuts the street, subject to DRC approval and case-by-case review. Under-eave lighting shall not be used as security lighting. Hardwired canned lighting installed into the soffit or ceiling of the front porch shall light only the front porch and not extend beyond that area. Under-eave hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems or hardwired canned lighting can be installed under a roofed cover above a rear deck or rear patio, subject to DRC approval and case-by-case review, if the light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or onto the street and the light is warm, with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less. During non-holiday lighting periods, under-eave lighting must be warm white, static, and must not strobe, flash, pulse, chase, or use patterns outside approved architectural accent lighting. A homeowner may install traditional under-eave lighting, or use track lighting systems in a static pattern to accent the home architecturally. All under-eave lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. Decorative lighting must consist of cafe, globe, or lit rope style lights; LED string lights, holiday-decoration-style string lights, and other forms of lighting are not allowed as decorative lighting. Rear decorative lighting does not require DRC approval if located under a roofed cover above a rear deck or patio, if the light cone does not cause glare, and if it is warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less. Landscape lighting must be low-level, downward-facing, warm white, and no taller than 36 inches for permitted solar in-ground lighting; no more than eight such fixtures are permitted in the front yard. Seasonal decorative lighting may include hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting, hardwired track eave/rake lighting, or temporary string lighting installed for the approved seasonal period. Seasonal decorative lighting should not create light trespass beyond property boundaries or glare onto surrounding properties. Temporary string lighting should use low-wattage lights; LED preferred. Seasonal decorative lighting may use colors and patterns and may blink, flash, chase, or strobe. Install and energize seasonal decorative lighting during the following approved seasonal lighting periods: from June 18 to July 7 and from October 1 through January 31. Outside those periods, temporary string lighting and clips must be removed, and hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting and hardwired track eave/rake lighting must be returned to the settings allowed in the under-eave lighting section. The CAB may extend removal dates due to extreme weather or other factors, but lighting may not be energized during that time. All holiday lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. Security lighting must be directed at the ground and house, must stay within property boundaries, must not cause glare to other properties, cannot be on 24/7 except for the front of the home facing the public street, and must be photocell-controlled and motion-activated so it cannot stay on longer than five minutes once activated. Security lighting may be installed on the rear of the home if it backs up to open space, but is not permitted in the rear if the open space is a designated wildlife corridor.

text: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Updated Exterior Lighting Policy Approved May 17, 2024 1. Landscape should only be used to provide such as walking paths, retaining walls, steps, etc. All landscape lights should be kept to a minimum. 2. Up-lighting is not an approved Dark Sky lighting type and is not permitted. Lights must have a downward-facing cone of light. 3. Lighting must be warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred). Colored lighting is not allowed. 4. Solar in-ground lighting is permitted in front and rear yards without DRC approval provided that: i. No light fixture shall exceed 36 inches in height. ii. Placement of fixtures is limited to edges of walks, driveways, and planting beds. iii. The light "cone" is downward facing and does not glare onto surrounding properties or the street. iv. No more than eight such fixtures shall be permitted in the front yard. 5. In the rear transition zone, solar in-ground down lighting, provided that it is less than 36 inches in height, is placed along the edges of walks or planting beds, and the cone of light is downward facing, not causing glare off of the property, is allowed. See Section 9-233 for additional transition zone guidelines. 6. All landscape lighting, with the exception of solar in-ground lighting, must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. -- 5 of 6 -- Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Updated Exterior Lighting Policy Approved May 17, 2024 e. Seasonal decorative lighting. Seasonal decorative lighting may include hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting, hardwired track eave/rake lighting, or temporary string lighting installed for the approved seasonal period. 1. Seasonal decorative lighting should be installed or operated in a manner that does not create any light trespass beyond the property boundaries or glare onto surrounding properties. 2. If using temporary string lighting, use low-wattage string lights; LED preferred. 3. Seasonal decorative lighting may be of various colors and patterns and is permitted to blink, flash, chase, or strobe. 4. Install and energize seasonal decorative lighting during the following approved seasonal lighting periods: From June 18 to July 7 and from October 1 through January 31. Outside of these approved seasonal lighting periods, all temporary string lighting and light installation clips are required to be removed, and all hardwired soffit installed lighting and hardwired track eave/rake lighting must be returned to the settings allowed in Section B above. 5. At the sole discretion of the CAB, removal dates for seasonal decorative lighting may be extended due to extreme weather conditions or other factors. During this time lighting may not be energized. 6. All holiday lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. f. Security Lighting. This type of lighting is installed for area lighting for security purposes. It includes wall-mounted fixture lighting, as well as floodlights and spotlights to illuminate portions of the lot for security purposes. 1. Security lighting must be directed at the ground and house. 2. The light cone must stay within the property boundaries. 3. The light source shall not cause glare to other properties. 4. Lighting, except for that on the front of the home and facing the public street, shall conform to the following guidelines: i. Lights cannot be on 24/7. ii. Lights must be on photocell control and motion activated. Once activated by motion, the lighting setting must be adjusted so it cannot stay on longer than five minutes. 5. Spotlights, floodlights, or other similar lights used for security applications may only be used on front porches, over garage doors, or over rear porches/decks. 6. Security Lighting may be installed at the rear of the home if it backs up to an open space. Lighting will not be permitted in the rear if the open space is a designated wildlife corridor. -- 6 of 6 --

summaryText: Resolution No. 2024-11-02, adopted November 22, 2024, amends the CAB Code effective immediately. Section 21-22(b)(101), Trash Containers: Trash shall not be stored or allowed to accumulate on any property except within appropriate containers, which shall be properly stored in an enclosed structure, the garage, or appropriately screened from view behind the wing fence. Section 21-22(b)(63), Outdoor Decorative Objects: Rear yard DRC approval is not required for yard or lawn ornamentation in the rear yard when ornamentation does not exceed three feet in height; DRC approval is required over three feet. Front yard DRC approval is not required for yard or lawn ornamentation only when there are no more than three ornaments, items are placed on the ground, items do not exceed 12 inches in height or width, and items are integrated into the landscape design; DRC approval is required for front-yard ornaments that do not meet those provisions. summaryText: Resolution No. 2025-06-01 establishes an amended and restated collection process for delinquent utility, monthly, and covenant enforcement fees and supersedes prior collection policies. Late Notice Letter: if unpaid on the 15th calendar day after due date, Provider sends a Late Notice Letter and charges a Late Notice Letter Fee. A partial payment towards any outstanding CAB Fees or Delinquent Fees for a Delinquent Account will not prevent the CAB from taking the provided next step to notify Property owners to bring current Delinquent Accounts or prevent the imposition of a subsequent fee, charge, or the application of interest as provided for herein or other interest, associated with the remaining amount due. d. Effect of Disputed Payments. If the Account Holder has explicitly directed application of a partial payment in writing and in conjunction with an appeal or dispute of a CAB Fee as provided under the Code of Rules for the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board, the Provider shall so credit the Account. Prepayment. A Property owner may prepay a CAB Fee. Any such prepayment shall create a credit balance on the Property’s account and Fees imposed shall be deducted from the credit balance. If the credit balance is not sufficient to pay a CAB Fee in full, the remaining balance of the Fee shall be paid prior to the CAB Fee payment’s due date. Any overpayment of an outstanding CAB Fee or overpayment of a Delinquent Account’s Delinquent Fees shall be considered as a prepayment and be credited to the Property’s account. 7. Payment Plans. a.
